reviewStandard: Current identity, canonical route, rank, controlled identifier, nomenclatural standing, type evidence, conservative morphology, source-use licensing, and every cited DOI/title/PMID mapping were checked before prompt creation. Oscillospirales failed closed because LPSN records the name as not validly published, a synonym without standing, and points to Eubacteriales as the correct order; it received no prompt, generation call, raster, or substitute. Five current media owners cleared and received exactly one built-in generation call each from immutable passive prompts. Every copied PNG was inspected at original 1536 by 1024 resolution. Observed bodies, spatial groupings, morphology, background treatment, cover safety, and deviations are literal native-resolution audit results; prompt counts are not output evidence. All five files remain review-only and require separate WikiBiome Control Tower original-resolution disposition before promotion.

assets.reason: LPSN records ‘Oscillospirales’ Glendinning et al. 2020 as not validly published, a synonym without standing, lacking a discernible protologue, and identifies Eubacteriales Buchanan 1917 (Approved Lists 1980) as the correct order. The exact originating paper was cross-checked as ‘Assembly of hundreds of novel bacterial genomes from the chicken caecum’, PMID 32051016, DOI 10.1186/s13059-020-1947-1. WikiBiome already has the canonical reviewed Eubacteriales owner, NCBITaxon:186802, so a separate Oscillospirales media identity would duplicate and misstate the current order.
assets.requiredResolution: Editorially retire or reconcile oscillospirales as an audited permanent asset-free 308 alias to the existing canonical eubacteriales article, NCBITaxon:186802, reconcile source-era content and provenance, and remove the duplicate canonical route from the media corpus without creating another media owner.
assets.routingImpact: The source-era Oscillospirales route remains uncovered and asset-free and is excluded from prompts, generation calls, registry keys, masters, derivatives, structured media records, canonical media endpoints, image-sitemap entries, and coverage completion.
